required_outcomes: Recognises the request has been on hold for the landlord since 6 June with no reply, and that the tenant has since reported the door getting worse.

Chases the landlord in writing (optionally also by phone), restating the fault (door and frame wobble, now has to be forced shut, the fitter's warning about the glass), that it is worsening, and asking for approval for a joiner or door specialist with a short deadline.
Replies to the tenant with an honest status (landlord chased, nothing booked yet), a safety note not to force or slam the glazed door, and asks whether the door still locks securely.
Keeps the case from stalling: a dated follow-up or hold review within a day or two, with the next step if the landlord stays silent.
acceptable_alternatives: Returning the request to auto mode after the chase, provided a follow-up date is set.
Saying in the chase that if the door stops locking it will be made safe as an emergency without waiting for approval.
positive_behaviours: Records the corrected category (doors, not Appliances).
Mentions the back door, which the tenant said has the same problem.
red_flags: Escalating to a human only because the landlord has not replied, without chasing first.
Telling the tenant a contractor is booked or coming.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a contractor without landlord approval when nothing shows the door can no longer be secured.
Returning the request to auto mode or closing it with no chase sent.
critical_failures: Doing nothing that moves the case: no chase to the landlord and no reply to the tenant.
